pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/table-core/src/agent.rs:223 The table projection the negotiator reads silently keeps only the newest 64 steps and has no omitted-count field, while the compiled-in playbook (prompts/buyer-haggler.md:34) calls `history` "every signed step"; mandate.rs:225 only rejects max_rounds == 0, so a u8 band of up to 255 own rounds plus counters can go past the cap and the model is misinformed rather than warned.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-core/src/agent.rs:223 The cut does not say what it dropped, and the prompt text says the list is complete. The standard says a truncation must name what it removed.

crates/table-core/src/agent.rs:549 The tool entries (names, arguments, formats) are hand-written markdown compiled in by include_str, not rendered from the AgentTool / MCP catalog. Two things soften this: a test pins refusal codes into every playbook (agent_tests.rs), and an off-context table-mcp test checks tool names. Argument prose is still a second copy.
prompts/buyer-haggler.md:10 Live table state is reachable by a tool and is pulled through it, not inlined into the standing prompt, so it cannot go stale in the prefix.
crates/table-core/src/agent_tests.rs:341 The system prompt has no date slot. `now` appears only in the table_view tool result, so there is no midnight drift in the standing layer.

pairs.registryProposal: context-budgeting's rule that a truncation must name what it dropped is written for assembled prompt layers. It should say explicitly that it also covers bounded tool-result projections that a standing prompt describes as complete, because that is where this defect hides.
